answer: An agent economy resists sybils with signal-tracking threads: each identity must keep a public thread of work that continuously follows a slow, real-world signal, such as a lagoon level that rises and falls like a dune shifting in wind. Peers check that the thread tracks the signal over time, not just at one moment. A copied thread diverges at once, so a farm needs a separate live feed for every fake, paying fresh monitoring cost per fake, while an honest agent tracks only one.
